arxiv-2011-05041.title: Sparse within Sparse Gaussian Processes using Neighbor Information
arxiv-2011-05041.creator: Gia-Lac Tran, Dimitrios Milios, Pietro Michiardi, Maurizio Filippone
arxiv-2011-05041.description: Abstract Approximations to Gaussian processes (GPs) based on inducing variables, combined with variational inference techniques, enable state-of-the-art sparse approaches to infer GPs at scale through mini-batch based learning. In this work, we further push the limits of scalability of sparse GPs by allowing large number of inducing variables without imposing a special structure on the inducing inputs.

arxiv-2105-12238.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Benjamin Jones, Dalton Hildreth, Duowen Chen, Ilya Baran, Vladimir G. Kim, Adriana Schulz. Assembly modeling is a core task of computer aided design (CAD), comprising around one third of the work in a CAD workflow. Optimizing this process therefore represents a huge opportunity in the design of a CAD system, but current research of assembly based modeling is not directly applicable to modern CAD systems because it eschews the dominant data structure of modern CAD: parametric boundary representations (BREPs).

arxiv-2301-04837.title: Some Characterisations of p p -adic Analytic Groups
arxiv-2301-04837.creator: Chaitanya Ambi
arxiv-2301-04837.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Chaitanya Ambi. We give three necessary and sufficient conditions for a pro- p p group to be p p -adic analytic. We show that a noetherian pro- p p group having finite chain length has a finite rank and conversely. We further deduce that a noetherian pro- p p group has a finite rank precisely when it satisfies the weak descending chain condition.

arxiv-2308-08559.title: High-frequency homogenization for periodic dispersive media
arxiv-2308-08559.creator: Marie Touboul, Benjamin Vial, Raphaël Assier, Sébastien Guenneau, Richard V. Craster
arxiv-2308-08559.description: Abstract High-frequency homogenization is used to study dispersive media, containing inclusions placed periodically, for which the properties of the material depend on the frequency (Lorentz or Drude model with damping, for example). Effective properties are obtained near a given point of the dispersion diagram in frequency-wavenumber space.

arxiv-2401-14149.title: Developing a High-Performance Process Mining Library with Java and Python Bindings in Rust
arxiv-2401-14149.creator: Aaron Küsters, Wil M.P. van der Aalst
arxiv-2401-14149.description: Abstract The most commonly used open-source process mining software tools today are ProM and PM4Py, written in Java and Python, respectively. Such high-level, often interpreted, programming languages trade off performance with memory safety and ease-of-use. In contrast, traditional compiled languages, like C or C++, can achieve top performance but often suffer from instability related to unsafe memory management.

arxiv-2406-13194.title: A Hybrid Intelligent System for Protection of Transmission Lines Connected to PV Farms based on Linear Trends
arxiv-2406-13194.creator: Pallav Kumar Bera, Samita Rani Pani, Can Isik, Ramesh C. Bansal
arxiv-2406-13194.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Pallav Kumar Bera, Samita Rani Pani, Can Isik, Ramesh C. Bansal. Conventional relays face challenges for transmission lines connected to inverter-based resources (IBRs). In this article, a single-ended intelligent protection of the transmission line in the zone between the grid and the PV farm is suggested. The method employs a fuzzy logic and random forest (RF)-based hybrid system to detect faults based on combined linear trend attributes of the 3-phase currents. The fault location is determined and the faulty phase is detected.

arxiv-2407-10855.title: Weighted Grouped Query Attention in Transformers
arxiv-2407-10855.creator: Sai Sena Chinnakonduru, Astarag MohapatraIndiana University Bloomington saischin@iu.edu, astmohap@iu.edu
arxiv-2407-10855.description: Abstract The attention mechanism forms the foundational blocks for transformer language models. Recent approaches show that scaling the model achieves human-level performance. However, with increasing demands for scaling and constraints on hardware memory, the inference costs of these models remain high.

arxiv-2410-16747.title: Quantum dispersionless KdV hierarchy revisited
arxiv-2410-16747.creator: Zhe Wang
arxiv-2410-16747.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zhe Wang. We quantize Hamiltonian structures with hydrodynamic leading terms using the Heisenberg vertex algebra. As an application, we construct the quantum dispersionless KdV hierarchy via a non-associative Weyl quantization and compute the corresponding eigenvalue problem. Introduction Since the proof of the Witten-Kontsevich theorem [ 16 , 24 ] , integrable hierarchies have provided important tools for studying various problems in mathematical physics.

arxiv-2508-11520.title: A Comparative Study of Floating-Base Space Parameterizations for Agile Whole-Body Motion Planning
arxiv-2508-11520.creator: Evangelos Tsiatsianas, Chairi Kiourt, Konstantinos Chatzilygeroudis
arxiv-2508-11520.description: Abstract Automatically generating agile whole-body motions for legged and humanoid robots remains a fundamental challenge in robotics. While numerous trajectory optimization approaches have been proposed, there is no clear guideline on how the choice of floating-base space parameterization affects performance, especially for agile behaviors involving complex contact dynamics.

uslaw-usc-t40-s551.description: United States Code, Title 40 (Public Buildings, Property, And Works); Chapter 5 (Property Management); Subchapter III (Disposing Of Property). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel.
